column1: # What each recording may be compared as, declared rather than discovered.
# A step writes its expectations against one census. That is a claim about
#   STABLE  byte-identical across runs; a raw-text expectation is sound
#   ORDER   same lines, different order; compare as a multiset, never as text
#   VALUE   the content itself moves; expectations may name shape only --
#           schema, row counts, column names, sentinel lines, exit status
# THIS DECLARATION IS FOR RECORDINGS TAKEN AT CORES=1, and it is the second
# one. The first was derived from r14/r15 and read 99 STABLE / 8 ORDER / 10
# VALUE: seventeen jobs that could not carry a raw-text expectation. Fifteen of
# those seventeen were a *width* -- 58 of the 78 main classes call
# setMaster("local[*]"), which is availableProcessors(), so the recordings were
# taken at whatever the box happened to have and the partitions were combined in
# whatever order the threads happened to finish (NOTES 4.5). Pinning
# -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=1 in both runners takes r18 and r19 to 115 of 117
# byte-identical, at the same coverage to the line and about 20% more wall.
# Two survive, and neither is a width: an unseeded sample() and an upstream
# aligner that writes into its inputs. Those keep their mechanism note below;
# the fifteen that were rescued carry "(needs the pinned width)" so that nobody
# The classes are about *one rung*: "across runs" here means across runs of the
# same build. A job may be STABLE by this file and still move from Spark 3.4 to
# Spark 3.5, and two of them do -- DatasetClassifier and PdbToUniProtMappingDemo
# are STABLE below, correctly, and are also projected, as class RUNG in
# pkg/suite/projection.tsv, because the line that moves across rungs moves for
# a mechanism no migration guide documents (NOTES 4.9.1 and 4.10.3). Do not read
# STABLE as "a step may score this whole recording as text": read it as "within
# a rung, the bytes are the bytes". projection.py --selftest asserts that every
# RUNG row names a job declared STABLE here, so the two files state the two
# halves and neither can quietly absorb the other's job.
# stability.py re-derives the class from two or more census directories and
# fails when an observation is worse than the declaration here. The unsafe
# direction is the only one that fails: a job declared STABLE that moves would
# have been scored on text that does not hold, whereas a job declared VALUE
# that happens to agree twice has cost nothing. NOTES 1.8 and 4.5.
# One consequence is worth having on purpose: run stability.py against an
# *unpinned* pair and it fails, loudly, on those fifteen. The declaration is
# therefore also the detector for a replay that forgot to set CORES.
# It is now derived twice over, and the file is sorted by job, so the two
# derivations are interleaved rather than stacked. 117 of the 140 rows come
# from r18/r19 as described above. The other 23 -- the fourteen CLI reject
# recipes and the nine new harness subcommands -- come from r22/r23, the first
# pair of censuses to carry all 140 jobs, on mmtf-record:3. Every one of the 23
# was observed byte-identical, and the nine harness subcommands -- which also
# ran in r21 -- were observed byte-identical across all three. No job declared
# here has ever been observed worse than its declaration.
# Two of the 23 record nothing: their recipe is rejected before the job prints
# anything, so their .norm is empty and their answer is the exit status alone.
# An empty file is byte-stable for a reason that has nothing to do with the
# job, so those two carry a mechanism note instead of a bare dash; a step that
# scores them on text is scoring a tautology.
